current.text: Josh ranks Washington 125 to 150 in category leagues. He sees no path to a top 80 finish because Dallas has so many forwards. In a 12 team league he would only take him in round 14 or later.
Josh projects Washington to start, with Kyrie Irving, Max Christie, Cooper Flagg and Morez Johnson Jr.
Dallas has a crowded frontcourt. Almost every player besides Kyrie Irving is a power forward, and Washington competes for minutes with Lively, Gafford, Johnson Jr., Aldama and Naji Marshall.
Dusty May is the new head coach. Nobody knows yet how he will split the minutes among the centers and forwards like Washington.
Lively, Dharma and Morez Johnson Jr. are hurt. That leaves Gafford as the likely opening night center.
Dallas plays 4 games in each of our three playoff weeks, which is probably the best playoff schedule in the league. It also has a league-high 16 back-to-backs.

durable.text: Washington is very streaky, with hot streaks and ice-cold slumps. His shooting goes up and down, and lately it has been down.

note: Washington sits right at our 144 player cutoff: Yahoo ranks him 133, ESPN 151 and Josh 125 to 150. Both sites price him at 0 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season, so he is a 1 USD bench pick at most and is often available on waivers. His small plus is rebounds and blocks (6.7 and 1.0 projected), but about 45% FG and 70% FT give away some value. Early in the season, check whether he starts under Dusty May while Lively and Johnson Jr. are hurt. Dallas plays 4-4-4 in our playoff weeks, which makes him a useful pickup later in the season.
